parts: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a), where F is an antiderivative. The constant C cancels. With a substitution, change the limits too.
As the limit of a sum: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = lim h→0 h[f(a) + f(a + h) + … + f(a + (n − 1)h)], with nh = b − a.
∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x)dx; ∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x)dx. ∫₋ₐᵃ f(x)dx = 2∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx if f is even, and 0 if f is odd. Split the integral where |…| changes sign.
Typical use: I = ∫₀^(π/2) cos³x/(sin³x + cos³x)dx. Replacing x by π/2 − x gives the same with sin and cos swapped; adding, 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.
Area under y = f(x) from a to b (f ≥ 0) = ∫ₐᵇ y dx. Area between two curves = ∫ₐᵇ (upper − lower) dx, with a and b the x-coordinates of the intersections.
